clue.text: Explosion registered over a thousand kilograms across island

indicators.note: in a down-to-up sense, over tells us to read the word for registered from right to left

parts.note: registered means noted

indicators.note: across means the thousand-kilogram unit is stretched over the island letter

parts.note: a metric ton is a thousand kilograms

explanation.surface: A blast was measured at over a tonne of explosive somewhere on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' in a down-to-up sense reads the registered word backwards; 'across' means the ton straddles the island letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonation is a loud blast, a synonym for explosion.

clue.text: Carrier's no good close to island, beginning to ground

parts.note: duff is slang for useless or no good
Elba is the Italian island of Napoleon's exile

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A useless carrier lands on an island near the start of its descent.
explanation.definitionFit: A duffel bag is a cylindrical canvas carrier.

clue.text: Had an idea, however daft, finally

parts.note: though means however

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word daft

explanation.surface: Someone came up with a notion, silly though it was in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought is the past of think, meaning had an idea.

clue.text: Everything about weak king is a cue for renewed action

parts.note: all means everything
C is circa, about
Shakespeare's King Lear is a feeble old king

explanation.surface: With the king feeble, everyone waits for a signal to act again.
explanation.definitionFit: The all-clear is a signal that danger is over and normal activity may resume.

clue.text: Tsar I haven't clued?

indicators.note: clued signals that the preceding words are the result of the setter's wordplay, so the solver works backwards to it

parts.note: these clue words are what you get by rearranging the tsar's first two words terribly, the second word acting as the anagram signal

explanation.surface: A setter admits failing to write a clue.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer's first two words with 'terrible' as anagram signal give I HAVEN'T; 'clued' says that is how the setter clued it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan IV of Russia, known as the Terrible, was the first ruler crowned tsar.

clue.text: Never once row about wife?

indicators.note: about tells us the row word surrounds the wife letter

parts.note: a row is a noise or din

explanation.surface: A couple who never once argued.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowise is an old word meaning in no way, never.

clue.text: Appear amazed when source of wine's run out

indicators.note: run out says the run letter is removed from the fruit

parts.note: grapes are what wine is made from
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone gawps in shock on finding the wine has run dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run out' looks like a phrase about the wine running dry; here R (run) goes 'out' of GRAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to stare open-mouthed, which is how amazement looks.

clue.text: Girl at bar ordered port

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman at a pub orders a glass of port.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibraltar is a port on the southern tip of Spain.

clue.text: Mole interrupted by a certain person arriving early

indicators.note: the mole word is broken into by the other piece

parts.note: a mole is a harbour pier or breakwater
one means a certain, as in one day

explanation.surface: A mole, the burrowing kind, disturbed by somebody coming early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' looks like the animal; it is a harbour breakwater.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is among the first to arrive somewhere or try something.

clue.text: Charge about American plot to annex a fleet

indicators.note: to annex is to tack something on, so the A is added at the end
about tells us the charge word goes round the plot word

parts.note: to charge a glass is to fill it
in American usage a lot is a plot of land

explanation.surface: A plot by a US agent to seize a whole fleet of ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet of ships or boats.

clue.text: Modern record repository we left in Slough

indicators.note: in means the left letter is placed inside the slough word

parts.note: a slough is a bog or swamp

explanation.surface: We lost a modern archive somewhere in the swamp, or in the town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is also an English town west of London, which the capital letter exploits; here it is a mire.
explanation.definitionFit: A weblog, or blog, is an online journal where up-to-date entries are kept.

clue.text: Consequently one may read it in Mother Goose

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the words that follow, across the gap

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme reader spots a Latin word in the children's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, used in English to mean consequently.

clue.text: One indolently forgetting everything as roulette is played

indicators.note: a game being played moves things about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gambler loses all track of time while the roulette wheel spins.
explanation.walkthrough: In Homer's Odyssey the lotus-eaters ate a fruit that made them forget home and live in idle bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotus-eater is a person living in dreamy indolence, after the forgetful islanders in Homer.

clue.text: A man of few words

parts.note: usually a taciturn person, read instead as an actor given only a handful of lines in a play

explanation.definitionFit: A bit player is an actor with a minor part, speaking only a few lines.

clue.text: What eliminates bugs from bad PC edits with one key

indicators.note: bad means the letters come out wrong, rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Bad edits on a PC remove software bugs with one keystroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesticide kills insects, which are informally called bugs.

clue.text: Endless computer memory minutes makes one rage

indicators.note: endless means the memory word loses its final letter

parts.note: a store is a computer's memory

explanation.surface: A computer that keeps running out of memory has its user fuming.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm is to rage loudly and angrily, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Fine spray allowed one to get rid of new parasite

parts.note: mist is a fine spray of droplets
let means allowed

indicators.note: the one word sheds its new letter

parts.note: taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: Fine spray kills off a fresh parasite.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistletoe is a parasitic plant growing on trees.

clue.text: Flier sporting communist emblem on top of tunic

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: the red star is a symbol of communism

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An airman wears a communist badge on his tunic.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird, so a flier.

clue.text: Entertainer in pursuit of good spirit

indicators.note: following behind, so the entertainer word comes after the good letter

parts.note: a host entertains guests

explanation.surface: A party host chasing after a decent drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is a spirit of the dead.

clue.text: Space behind front door where one's stowed ancient bag

indicators.note: something stowed is put away inside, so the ancient word goes inside

parts.note: a hall is the room just inside a front door
old means ancient

explanation.surface: An old bag kept in the hallway.
explanation.definitionFit: A holdall is a large soft bag for carrying belongings.

clue.text: Actor's character making Times rude in review

indicators.note: a review goes over things again, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A critic's notice in The Times is rude about a performer's role.
explanation.walkthrough: Demetrius is one of the young lovers in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Demetrius is a role played by actors in Shakespeare's comedy, so it is an actor's character.

clue.text: Popular and healthier way of taking drugs

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
haler is an old word for healthier, from hale

explanation.surface: A trendy, healthier way to take medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaler is a device for breathing in medicine.

clue.text: Sensible clothing we introduced to fashion-conscious youths

indicators.note: the we piece is put into the youths word

parts.note: Teds, Teddy boys, were stylish British youths of the 1950s

explanation.surface: We bring practical clothes to trendy teenagers.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweeds are hard-wearing woollen garments, practical country wear.

clue.text: English book Nullarbor and Serengeti?

definitions.meaning: a title on writing clear English: Sir Ernest Gowers's guide for civil servants
names of vast flat grasslands, in Australia and Tanzania, so terms for open country

explanation.surface: A book on English mentions two famous plains.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain Words is Gowers's classic book on English style, and the names given are words for plains.

clue.text: Out of hospital, boy's returning pulse

indicators.note: returning means the assembled letters are read backwards
boy's is read as boy has, so the boy word holds the hospital letter

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy discharged from hospital comes back to have his pulse taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 's (has) puts H inside LAD to make LAHD, and 'returning' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dhal is a dish of lentils or split peas, which are pulses.

clue.text: Shortage of good brandy — it's coming round in the morning

indicators.note: coming round means the brandy word encircles the morning letters

parts.note: fine is a high-quality French brandy
AM means in the morning

explanation.surface: Short of decent brandy, someone comes round groggily the next morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A famine is an acute shortage, especially of food.

clue.text: Duo awarded contract to form band

parts.note: a brace is a pair
to let a contract is to award it

explanation.surface: A double act is signed up to form a musical group.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is a band worn round the wrist.

clue.text: What's reported did make current Conservative depressed

definitions.meaning: the colour of Britain's Conservative party, used for a Tory

indicators.note: what is reported is what is heard spoken, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: blew means made a current of air

explanation.surface: A news story about a Tory politician feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of the UK Conservative Party, so a Tory is a blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means both a Conservative and feeling low, two separate senses.

clue.text: Has-been is put in post without power for the church

indicators.note: without means outside, so the post word goes round the power letter

parts.note: a letter put in the post is sent
taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A washed-up figure is posted to a powerless church job.
explanation.definitionFit: A spent force is someone whose power or influence is gone, a has-been.
